desc.SEVEN: numeral-7 hook, thin or bold with a long top bar and hooked foot, and the bold caret (v2 SEVEN/SEVENB/CARET merged in v3)
desc.OMEGABAR: omega/w with or without a bar on top (v2 OMEGABAR/OMEGA2 merged in v3; key: null N10)
desc.SIX: 6 / b, loop at base with ascender (key: n1/n2)
desc.TWO: numeral 2: round, flat/Z-shaped or D-shaped (v2 TWO/TWOFLAT/DEE merged in v3)
desc.EIGHTBAR: 8 crossed by a bar (NOT in key)
desc.XCURL: cursive x with curled ends (NOT in key; key d zigzag?)
desc.THETA: circle crossed by a horizontal bar (NOT in key)
desc.HCURL: H-shape with curled serifs (key: word code under Prince of Castile, per the image; N4 per pass A)
desc.LL: two verticals on a baseline (NOT in key)
desc.ENN: bold N (NOT in key; or N6)
desc.PHI: phi loop on a descender, crossed (key: a)
desc.TEE: t-like cross with a curl, or a plus with a foot (key: b = T? or t)
desc.HOOK: small hook-and-loop family: script e, bold e, rho/long-s with loop, t-cross with loop, u-curl, mu (v2 codes ELOOP/ECAP/RHO/TLOOP/UCURL/MU merged in v3: H3 passes could not separate them)
desc.JHOOK: bold vertical stroke turning left at the foot, a J without a top bar (H29b/H30, 28 Sept 2026: both Opus readers flagged it as outside the atlas at L1.18, L1.21, L3.30; NOT in key)
desc.EPSILON: bold epsilon opening RIGHT (L8.4; H15 called it EREV, both Opus readers in H29c read it as an ordinary epsilon, not reversed; key: null N8 is a capital E, N9 the reversed E -- which of the two this is stays M)
desc.EREV: reversed capital E -- superseded in v4 by EPSILON for L8.4 (H30)
